# Other processors and machines

*README.MD file mostly generated by Anthropic's Claude AI because Thomas Dzubin hates documenting code.  LOL*

This folder holds everything that is not the Elf: descriptions of other processors for the assembler and
the listing tools (6502, 8080, Z80, 6800, 6803, 6809), two CPU cores (the Motorola MC6803 and a Zilog Z80
skeleton), the MC6847 video chip and the TRS-80 MC-10 built from them, with their tests, notes and tools.
It is kept apart so the Elf stays small and in focus: **none of it is in the firmware or the desktop builds
and no Elf file includes or calls anything here** (the Elf's `isa.h` knows only the 1802). Work on it
resumes later. `othercpus.h` includes all of its headers; add `-Iothercpus` to the include path.

Notes in this folder: `STATUS.md` (what is finished and what is next), `RESEARCH.md` (sources and choices),
`CHANGELOG.md`, `CLAUDE.md` (the file guide).

## Files

```
othercpus.h               includes everything below
isa_others.h              the isa_t declarations of the descriptions below
isa_6502.c isa_8080.c isa_z80.c isa_6800.c (6800 and 6803) isa_6809.c, each with its _const.h
                          the instruction-set descriptions (assembler, disassembler, flow)
cpu6803.c / .h            the Motorola MC6803 core (cpu6803_const.h)
cpuz80.c / .h             the Zilog Z80 core skeleton (cpuz80_const.h)
mc6847.c / .h             the MC6847 video chip (mc6847_const.h)
mc10.c / .h               the TRS-80 MC-10 (mc10_const.h)
tests/                    test_isa_others.c, test_cpu6803.c, test_mc6847.c, test_mc10.c, test_cpuz80.c,
                          vector_check.c
tools/mame_diff/          the scratch harness that compared the 6803 core with MAME's opcode code
run_tests.sh              builds and runs all the tests: sh othercpus/run_tests.sh (from the project folder)
```

The shared files they use from the project folder are `isa.h`, `asm_core.c`, `source_gen.c`, `membus.c`,
`rom.c`, `qaudio.c`, `machine.h`, `target.h` and `platform.h`. The tests need `-DASM_IMAGE_SIZE=0x5000` (the
MC-10 has 20 KB of RAM; the Elf's default is 16 KB).

## Processor descriptions

The tools are written to work for any processor. A processor is described by one `isa_t` (see `isa.h`):
how to write an instruction as text and which way the program goes after it (for the disassembler and the
code/data trace of the listing), how its numbers are spelled, and how to turn one line of assembly into
bytes (using the assembler's `asm_*` helpers for the operands). `isa_1802.c` is the one in use; the 6502,
8080, Z80, 6800, 6803 and 6809 have descriptions too (documented opcodes only, checked against an independent
instruction table), so a listing or an assembly of their code works today:

| Processor | Numbers | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 1802 | `2F` (hex), `#47` decimal, `$2F`, `2FH` | register names `R5`, RCA mnemonics, `DW` high byte first |
| 6502 | `$2F`, `%0101`, decimal | `LDA #$12`, `($12),Y`; `.W` forces absolute, `.B` zero page |
| 8080 | `2FH`, `0101B`, decimal | Intel mnemonics; `DW` low byte first |
| Z80 | `2FH`, `0101B`, decimal | Zilog mnemonics (`LD A,(IX+5)`, `EX AF,AF'`, `JR NZ,loop`); every documented opcode of the CB, ED, DD, FD and DD CB / FD CB groups; `RST 38H` takes the address; `DW` low byte first |
| 6800, 6803 | `$2F`, `%0101`, decimal | `LDAA`, `LDAB`; `.W` forces extended; the 6803 adds `LDD`, `ADDD`, `MUL` and more |
| 6809 | `$2F`, `%0101`, decimal | all the indexed forms, `TFR`, `PSHS`; `<` and `>` force the short or long form |

To add one, write `isa_<name>.c` with its table in `isa_<name>_const.h`, add it to `tests/test_isa_others.c`'s list
(which then checks every opcode), and give a machine (CPU core, memory map, devices) to run it on.

The 6502's opcode table was also checked against the real chip's behaviour: `tests/vector_check.c` reads
the JSON files of the [SingleStepTests](https://github.com/SingleStepTests/65x02) 6502 vectors (the first
300 KB of each file is plenty) and checks that every instruction's length, branch target and jump target is
what the chip did:

```
gcc -Wall -Wextra -I. -Iothercpus -DASM_IMAGE_SIZE=0x5000 \
    othercpus/tests/vector_check.c othercpus/isa_6502.c asm_core.c -o vector_check
./vector_check 6502 a9.json b1.json ...
```

### The 6803 CPU core

`cpu6803.c` is a CPU core for the Motorola MC6803 (the processor of the TRS-80 MC-10): the whole 6800
instruction set with the 6801 additions, the data sheet's cycle count for every opcode, the interrupts
(IRQ, NMI, the on-chip timer and serial requests, WAI, SWI, the delay after CLI and TAP), the illegal-opcode
trap, and what is on the chip: 128 bytes of RAM at `$80`, four ports (through callbacks), and the 16-bit
timer with output compare (it drives P21) and input capture. `cpu6803_step()` runs one instruction and
returns its cycles; the caller keeps the rest of the machine in step by that. It is not used by a machine
yet, so it is not in the firmware's file lists. Its test:

```
gcc -Wall -Wextra -I. -Iothercpus -DASM_IMAGE_SIZE=0x5000 \
    othercpus/tests/test_cpu6803.c othercpus/cpu6803.c asm_core.c othercpus/isa_6800.c \
    -o test_cpu6803
./test_cpu6803
```

### The 6847 video chip

`mc6847.c` is the Motorola MC6847 video display generator (the MC-10's and the Color Computer's video chip):
32 x 16 text with the chip's built-in 64-character set, semigraphics 4 and 6, the "stripes" the chip makes of
external alphanumerics when there is no character ROM, and all eight graphics modes (64 x 64 up to 256 x 192),
with the chip's own addressing, the colours and the border. The machine tells it how many processor cycles went
by (`mc6847_advance()`, 57 cycles to a line, 262 lines to a frame) and sets the mode pins; at the end of each
line the chip records the pins and the bytes that line shows, so a mode change in the middle of a frame shows
from that line on. `mc6847_render_line()` turns a recorded line into 256 palette indices, and the lines that
changed are marked (`mc6847_take_dirty()`), so a screen redraws only those. Not in the firmware's file lists
until a machine uses it. Its test:

```
gcc -Wall -Wextra -I. -Iothercpus -DASM_IMAGE_SIZE=0x5000 \
    othercpus/tests/test_mc6847.c othercpus/mc6847.c -o test_mc6847
./test_mc6847
```

### The TRS-80 MC-10

`mc10.c` puts the 6803 core, the 6847 and the MC-10's memory map together (RAM at `$4000`, 4K or 20K; the one
hardware port at `$BFFF`; the ROM at `$E000`), with the keyboard matrix (`mc10_press_char()`, SHIFT held for
the shifted symbols), the video mode pins, the one-bit sound (into the same `qaudio` the Elf's Q line uses) and
the cassette lines of port 2. The 8K ROM is not part of this project: fit it as a `.ROM` file the way any ROM
image is fitted (file menu `R`, at `E000`); without one a small built-in program writes "NO MC-10 ROM FITTED" on
the screen. `mc10_run()` runs whole instructions and keeps the video chip in step by their cycles. It has no
screen on the PicoCalc yet (see `STATUS.md`), so it is not in the firmware's file lists. Its test:

```
gcc -Wall -Wextra -I. -Iothercpus -DASM_IMAGE_SIZE=0x5000 \
    othercpus/tests/test_mc10.c othercpus/mc10.c othercpus/cpu6803.c othercpus/mc6847.c \
    membus.c rom.c qaudio.c asm_core.c othercpus/isa_6800.c -o test_mc10
./test_mc10
```

Run the tests of the descriptions with:

```
gcc -Wall -Wextra -I. -Iothercpus -DASM_IMAGE_SIZE=0x5000 \
    othercpus/tests/test_isa_others.c asm_core.c source_gen.c othercpus/isa_6502.c \
    othercpus/isa_8080.c othercpus/isa_z80.c othercpus/isa_6800.c othercpus/isa_6809.c \
    -o test_isa_others
./test_isa_others
```

The Z80 core (`cpuz80.c`, a skeleton that runs the 8080's instruction set with the Z80's flags and T-states; the
JR group, EX AF,AF', EXX and the CB, DD, ED and FD groups are the next things to add) has its own test:

```
gcc -Wall -Wextra -I. -Iothercpus -DASM_IMAGE_SIZE=0x5000 \
    othercpus/tests/test_cpuz80.c othercpus/cpuz80.c asm_core.c othercpus/isa_z80.c \
    -o test_cpuz80
./test_cpuz80
```
